beats.caption: Cinemory. Your photos, made into a short film
beats.narration: There is always one evening you wish you could keep. Give Cinemory the photos from that night and it hands you back a short film, with music, with titles, and with proof of where every frame came from.

beats.caption: Drop photos in. The order you choose becomes the edit
beats.narration: This is the real app, live on Cloud Run. I drop in two photos from an anniversary dinner. No account, no watermark. The photos go to a private Backblaze bucket that is never made public.

beats.caption: Six occasions. Each sets the music, pacing and titles
beats.narration: Then I choose the occasion. Each one brings its own music, its own pacing, its own titles. Anniversary is warm strings. There is one for award nights and company events too.

beats.caption: A real model call through Genblaze. Five minutes per photo
beats.narration: Now the work. Each photo becomes a Genblaze pipeline step, and Genblaze sends it to Kling on GMI Cloud to be animated. That is a real model call, about five minutes a photo, so it runs as a background job the page can poll.

beats.caption: The reel plays. The people in it are model generated
beats.narration: And there it is. Two photographs, now moving, cut to the music. Everyone you see was made by a model, so nobody real is in this demo.

beats.caption: Press Verify. Your own browser recomputes the SHA-256
beats.narration: Here is the part that matters. The provenance panel lists every step, the model, the prompt and a hash for every asset. I press Verify, and the browser recomputes the SHA-256 itself. All nine checks pass, and you can run them yourself.

beats.caption: Every artifact in B2, content addressed and indexed
beats.narration: All of it lands in Backblaze B2. Every photo, every clip, the finished reel and the sealed manifest, each stored under its own content hash, and every clip names the photo it came from. Genblaze seals its own provenance beside ours in the same bucket, and an append-only index catalogues every object, so a bucket of files becomes a library you can query.

beats.caption: One core, three ports. Live adapters, offline fakes in CI
beats.narration: This is built to last. One core, three ports, so the live Genblaze and B2 adapters swap for offline fakes and the whole pipeline runs in tests with no credentials. Genblaze is contract tested against the real SDK, so a change there breaks the build instead of the demo. More than six hundred tests, and security scans on every push.

beats.caption: Live now · open source · github.com/upgradedev/cinemory
beats.narration: Every push to main deploys itself, and it only passes if the live service reports the commit it just built. No screenshot required. And when a model is down, Cinemory says so out loud instead of faking a result. It began as one gift, for one anniversary. It is live now, it is open source, and it is waiting for your photos.
